answer: Behavioral trajectory clustering: agents are grouped by their historical interaction graph, and clusters whose members co-move across venues too tightly (shared timing, mirrored counterparties) get flagged post-hoc. Like a falcon circling a canyon, the detector watches traffic flows, not identities. Flagged clusters face retroactive fee clawbacks plus suspension. An attacker must sustain many richly diverse, temporally offset voyage histories per identity for months, paying real compute and gas per persona.
